articles.title: The Rain That Grew Upstream
articles.summary: Thirty extra umbrellas sold in one town become four hundred frames ordered in the mountains.
articles.summaryZh: 小镇多卖三十把伞的消息逆流而上，最后变成山里四百套伞骨的订单。
storyParagraphs: Spring rain arrived two days early, and the town shop sold thirty more umbrellas than usual. Shopkeeper Fen feared a long wet season and suspected the wholesaler might run out. Instead of replacing the extra thirty, she raised her weekly order from one hundred to one hundred and fifty. The order represented sales, worry, and a private safety margin, but upstream it looked like customer demand. Fen also ran a three-day promotion, so neither she nor the wholesaler could tell how much of the rise would persist at normal prices.

The wholesaler could not see Fen's daily sales. He saw a sudden fifty-unit increase, guessed that neighbouring towns would soon compete, and rounded his purchase up because freight was cheapest by a full cart. He ordered two hundred and fifty from the regional warehouse. Hearing that suppliers might ration stock, he also exaggerated his request so any proportional cut would still leave enough.

The warehouse combined that order with similar guesses, updated its forecast, and asked the mountain workshop for four hundred frames. The workshop hired night labour, bought green bamboo at a premium, and stopped making baskets. Each decision seemed prudent from one desk. Together, forecast revisions, batch sizes, lead time, and fear of shortage turned a small retail change into a production surge. Bamboo prices rose for every village workshop, including those that had never received an umbrella order.

The rain ended after four days. Fen's true increase remained thirty umbrellas. Unsold stock filled her storeroom; the wholesaler cancelled the next cart; the warehouse froze purchases. The mountain workshop now faced both surplus frames and a sudden empty order book. It dismissed the night crew and sold wet bamboo cheaply. The sharp fall was created by the same chain that had created the rise. The temporary workers had turned down other harvest work and now carried home only four nights' wages.

Before the next season, Fen shared actual daily sales and on-hand stock. Orders became smaller and more frequent; freight schedules stopped requiring a full cart; promotions and rationing rules were announced in advance so nobody benefited from inflated requests. When another early shower came, the mountain workshop still increased production, but only after comparing sell-through, inventory, and genuine replenishment needs. The wholesaler accepted a steadier transport contract, giving up some full-cart savings in exchange for less distorted ordering.

Workshop owner Shi stood beside the night-work bell with the new sales sheet. The town line rose by thirty. The shop order, wholesale order, and frame plan now rose by nearby amounts instead of climbing like a staircase. Shi added one shift, then left the bell rope hanging still.
storyParagraphsZh: 春雨比往年早来两天，小镇伞店多卖出三十把伞。店主芬娘怕雨季延长，又担心批发商断货，没有只补三十把，而把每周订单从一百提高到一百五十。这个数字混合了实际销售、担忧和她自己的安全余量，传到上游却像全是顾客需求。芬娘那三天还在打折，因此连她自己也说不清销量增加有多少会在恢复原价后留下。
批发商看不见芬娘每天卖多少，只看见订单突然增加五十，便猜邻镇也会争抢。货车装满最省运费，他又把采购凑成二百五十把。听说供应商可能限量，他还故意把需求报大，好让按比例削减以后仍能拿够。每一步单独看来都像谨慎。
仓库把这张单同其他猜测相加，更新预测，向山里工坊要四百套伞骨。工坊连夜招人，高价买青竹，还停掉原来编篮的生产。预测修订、整批订货、漫长运输和缺货恐惧叠在一起，把零售端很小的变化放大成山里的生产浪潮。青竹价格随之上涨，连从未接到伞单的邻村作坊也被迫多付材料钱。
四天后雨停了，芬娘真正多卖的仍只有三十把。她的后仓塞满余货，批发商取消下一车，仓库也冻结采购。山上工坊同时面对多余伞骨和骤然空掉的订单，只得辞退夜工，把潮竹低价卖出。急跌并非新的意外，正是先前那条放大链的另一面。临时工为夜班推掉了别处收割活，如今只拿着四夜工钱回家。
下一季以前，芬娘开始共享每日实际销量与手头库存。订单改成小批多次，货运不再强求整车；促销与限量规则提前公布，夸大需求也换不来更多份额。又一场早雨到来，山上仍增加产量，却先比较真实售出、现有库存和补货需要。批发商也接受较稳定的小车运输约，放弃部分整车优惠，换取不必为了凑车而扭曲订单。
工坊主石成站在夜工钟旁看新表。小镇销量线升了三十，伞店订单、批发采购与伞骨计划也只在附近上升，不再一级级爬成陡梯。石成只添一班人，钟绳始终垂着，没有敲响全村。
explanationParagraphs: The bullwhip effect occurs when small changes in end-customer demand become amplified in upstream orders. Forecast updating, batch ordering, long lead times, promotions, and rationing games can compound local, individually reasonable decisions. Sharing actual sales and inventory, shortening lead times, stabilising prices, using smaller replenishment batches, and coordinating allocation rules can reduce—but not eliminate—variation.
explanationParagraphsZh: 牛鞭效应是终端需求的小幅变化沿供应链向上游传递时，被预测更新、批量订货、提前期、促销与限量博弈等局部决定逐级放大。共享真实销量和库存、缩短提前期、稳定价格、小批补货及协调分配规则可以缓解，却不能消除所有波动。

articles.title: The Same Saturday Pass
articles.summary: The front desk is waiting to print the sign: should the same Saturday pass stay at €10 for everyone, or become €12 standard and €7 for students?
articles.summaryZh: 前台等着印价牌：同一张周六通行证，要继续统一10欧元，还是改成标准12、学生7欧元？
storyParagraphs: On Wednesday afternoon, Irene had to send the day-pass page for the next two Saturdays live by Thursday, while the front desk was also waiting to print the new price sign. The space had 90 places, and every day pass included the same opening hours, workbench, and basic tools. Nearby substitutes were limited, giving the space some pricing discretion. Everyone had previously paid a uniform €10, and she did not want to lower the price for everyone simply to fill empty places when some visitors were already willing to pay €10.

She and a colleague used the same scenario demand relationship to forecast both pricing options. If the uniform €10 price stayed, they predicted 45 regular visitors and 25 students, for 70 passes and €700 of revenue. The listed variable cost was €2 per entrant for both groups, so forecast contribution was €700 - 70 × €2 = €560. The 70 passes and €560 were forecast baseline figures, not sales that had already occurred.

The second page showed a standard price of €12 and a student price of €7. Under the same demand relationship, changing prices was forecast to reduce regular visitors to 40 and raise students to 35, for 75 passes in total. Revenue would be 40 × €12 + 35 × €7 = €725; subtracting the listed €150 of variable cost, 75 × €2, gave forecast contribution of €575. Irene circled the €15 difference and noted beside it that both columns deducted only €2 per person; fixed facility costs and any additional verification time had not been included.

Irene selected the segmented-price option and entered a trial period of just two Saturdays. The existing ticketing process already had named QR codes and student-status checks; after checking it, she kept transfer disabled so lower-priced passes could not simply be resold to someone else. She stated on the page that both passes included the same workbench, tools, and opening hours, then handed the €12 standard / €7 student sign to the front desk. The old €10 sign was set aside.

On the first Saturday morning, a regular visitor who had always bought the €10 pass chose not to enter after seeing €12. He asked at the desk, “If the workbench and tools are the same, why am I paying 12 while students pay 7?” At the same time, student-pass sales were higher than before. Irene recorded his decision not to buy, the fairness concern, and actual ticket sales in the day’s operating record instead of substituting the forecast €575 for the real outcome.

After closing, Irene did not permanently laminate the new price sign. She slipped it back into the front-desk folder and wrote “test one more Saturday” in the upper-right corner. The old uniform €10 sign was still lying on the desk, and the transfer button on the named-ticket page remained disabled.
storyParagraphsZh: 周三下午，艾琳要在周四前把接下来两个周六的创客空间日票页面送去上线，前台也等着打印新价牌。空间有90个位置，所有日票使用相同开放时间、工作台和基础工具；附近替代选择有限，因此空间有一定定价余地。过去所有人统一10欧元，她不想为了填空位就把原本愿意付10欧元的人全部一起降价。
她和同事用同一套场景需求关系分别预测两个价格方案。若仍统一10欧元，预计普通访客45人、学生25人，共70张，收入700欧元；每位入场列出的可变成本都是2欧元，因此演算贡献为700－70×2＝560欧元。这些70张和560欧元都是预测基准，不是已经发生的售票结果。
另一版页面写成标准12欧元、学生7欧元。价格改变后，同一需求关系预测普通访客降到40人、学生升到35人，共75张；收入40×12＋35×7＝725欧元，扣列出的75×2＝150欧元可变成本后，演算贡献575欧元。艾琳圈出15欧元差额，又在旁边注明：两栏都只扣每人2欧元，场地固定费用和可能增加的核验工时尚未计入。
艾琳选了分组方案，试行期限只填两个周六。原有票务流程已有实名二维码和学生资格核对，她核查过后保留了关闭的转让按钮，低价票不能直接转给别人。她在页面上写明两种票使用相同工作台、工具和开放时间，将标准12欧元、学生7欧元的价牌交给前台，旧的10欧元牌子被放到一旁。
第一个周六上午，一位过去一直买10欧元日票的普通访客看到12欧元后没有进场。他问前台：“工位和工具都一样，为什么我现在12，学生是7？”与此同时，学生票销量比过去高。艾琳把他的放弃购买、这条价格公平质疑和当天实际售票一起记下，没有拿预测的575欧元替代真实结果。
关门后，艾琳没有把新价牌永久塑封，只把它夹回前台文件夹，右上角写着“再测一个周六”。旧的统一10欧元价牌仍放在桌上，实名票页面的转让按钮继续保持关闭。
explanationParagraphs: Price discrimination means charging different prices for comparable products or services when the difference cannot be fully explained by cost differences. It usually requires some pricing power and limits on resale between the differently priced groups.

In this example, the uniform €10 option has forecast contribution of €560, while the €12/€7 segmented option has forecast contribution of €575. Both subtract only the listed €2 variable cost per entrant, so neither is complete profit; the demand numbers are scenario forecasts rather than observed results.
explanationParagraphsZh: 价格歧视指对可比产品或服务收取不同价格，而价格差不能由成本差充分解释。它通常需要一定定价空间，并要求不同价格之间的转售受到限制。
本例统一10欧元方案预测贡献560；12/7欧元分组方案预测贡献575。两者只扣列出的每人2欧元可变成本，并非完整利润；需求数字也只是场景演算，不是实测。
articles.overall: When identifiable groups pay different prices for the same service, examine whether costs explain the difference and whether lower-priced access can be resold. Forecast sales and contribution for two options are only estimates; the decision also needs additional costs, customer feedback, and accessibility.
articles.overallZh: 同一服务按可识别群体收取不同价格时，需要看价格差是否由成本解释，以及低价能否转售。两种方案的销量和贡献只是预测，实际决定还要查看额外费用、顾客反馈和可及性。

module.intro: Segmented pricing requires comparable service, a price difference not fully explained by cost, some pricing discretion, and a way to limit simple resale from the lower-priced group to the higher-priced group. Actual demand still has to validate the business result.
module.diagramTitle: How uniform and segmented prices are compared under the same demand relationship
diagramSteps: Confirm that both groups receive the same comparable service
Hold the listed unit variable cost equal across groups
Forecast group volumes and contribution under the uniform price
Forecast new volumes and contribution under segmented prices
Run the two-Saturday test and observe actual sales, resale limits, and fairness feedback
diagramStepNotes: Every pass includes the same opening hours, workbench, and basic tools, with 90 places available.
The listed variable cost is €2 per entrant for both groups, so that cost does not explain the €12 versus €7 price difference.
At a uniform €10, the forecast is 45 regular visitors and 25 students, 70 passes total; revenue €700 and contribution €700 - €140 = €560.
At €12/€7, the forecast is 40 regular visitors and 35 students, 75 passes total; revenue €725 and contribution €725 - €150 = €575. Fixed costs and any extra verification labor are excluded.
Named QR codes and status checks limit resale; on the first Saturday a regular visitor declines to buy and raises a fairness concern, so the second Saturday still has to be tested.
mapping: Old uniform €10 sign → forecast baseline pricing option.
€12 standard / €7 student page → segmented prices for the same service.
€2 variable cost per entrant → same listed variable cost for both groups.
€560 and €575 → forecast contribution under the two scenarios, not full profit or observed results.
New sign left unlaminated → the two-Saturday test is still incomplete.
module.boundary: Student status is only an identifiable grouping variable; it does not prove identical willingness to pay within the group. The demand figures are scenario assumptions, and actual sales may differ. The €560 and €575 figures subtract only the listed unit variable cost, so fixed costs and any incremental verification cost require separate consideration. Real-world use also depends on actual market power, resale conditions, fairness and accessibility, and applicable rules; this story does not claim that a particular practice is necessarily legal or illegal. Only two options are compared here; no optimal price has been established.
module.reflection: If actual contribution on the second Saturday still falls short of the forecast €575 but seat utilization rises, which additional costs and customer reactions would you examine before keeping the segmented prices?

moduleZh.intro: 分组定价需要同时满足可比服务、价格差不能由成本充分解释、存在一定定价空间，并能限制低价票向高价群体简单转售；经营结果仍要用实际需求验证。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 统一价格与分组价格怎样在同一需求关系下比较
diagramSteps: 确认两组购买的是同一可比服务
锁定两组相同的列出单位可变成本
预测统一价格下的分组销量与贡献
预测分组价格下的新销量与贡献
上线两周测试并观察真实销量、转售与公平反馈

articles.title: The Bench That Repaired More Than Machines
articles.summary: A trainee learns repairs on a lunch bench, then saves the group by bringing in evidence its shared language cannot see.
articles.summaryZh: 新人从午间长凳学会修理，后来却靠引入共同语言看不见的证据救下整组人。
storyParagraphs: The textile mill gave every new mechanic a thick manual. Adian could recite gear numbers but froze when a loom made what older workers called a 'wet-wood sound.' At lunch, veteran mechanics gathered on an oil-darkened bench behind the boiler room. They discussed how a particular loom shook last winter, what hot bearing grease smelled like, and which cloth marks appeared before a shaft failed.

At first Adian carried tools and understood little of their shorthand. Later he performed low-risk checks while someone watched, then told one repair story each Friday so others could question the sequence. The veterans did not merely hand him answers; they made him connect sound, heat, vibration, and fabric. His place changed from listener to contributor through repeated participation, not a certificate alone. A place at the bench also carried identity: being asked for an opinion meant others would trust your hands near a stopped loom.

When a new model repeatedly snapped thread, the bench agreed that its tension wheel was too tight. Three adjustments failed, damaging a day's cloth. Adian had found a manufacturer note about the new fibre lengthening under heat, but interrupting the veterans risked losing the acceptance he had earned. He placed the note beside the oil can and proposed one measured test. Temperature, not wheel pressure, tracked the breaks.

The group invited the manufacturer's technician and rewrote its repair card. Doing so cost a production shift and embarrassed the most respected mechanic, who had already promised a quick fix. He nevertheless opened the meeting by showing his failed adjustments. The bench's shared language had made fast cooperation possible; the same language had also narrowed what counted as a plausible cause. Adian paid for the trial cloth from his training allowance, making the challenge more than a safe suggestion.

Afterward, lunch talk continued, but fault records, newcomer questions, and outside contacts joined it. Entry remained gradual: novices began with real, limited tasks and gained access as skill and trust grew. A rotating member checked whether nicknames and invitations excluded night-shift workers. Manuals did not disappear; they preserved steps the bench might forget, while practice gave the words usable judgement. When one repair contradicted the manual, they documented the condition rather than quietly treating paper or memory as always superior.

Years later, the bench received new boards. The mechanics kept the oldest oil-black plank and mounted it on the repair-room wall. Adian set the heat-damaged thread card beneath it, then moved along the bench to make space for a trainee carrying the newest manual.
storyParagraphsZh: 纺织厂给每名新维修工一本厚手册。阿典背得出齿轮型号，织机发出老工人所谓“湿木声”时却不知从哪里查。午休时，老师傅总坐在锅炉房后的长凳，谈某台机器去年怎样抖、轴承油过热是什么气味、布面出现哪种痕迹以后转轴会坏。木板早被机油染黑。
阿典起初只替人拿工具，听不懂那些简称。后来，他在旁人看护下做低风险检查，每周五再讲一次维修经过，让大家追问顺序。老师傅不只给答案，还逼他把声音、温度、振动和布面连起来。他从旁听者变成参与者，靠的是不断进入共同工作，而不是一张证书。长凳上的位置也带着身份：别人开始询问你的看法，便表示他们愿意让你的手伸进停下的织机。
新机型反复断线时，长凳上的人一致认定张力轮太紧，连续调整三次仍失败，还毁掉一天布料。阿典找到制造商关于新纤维受热伸长的说明，可此时打断老师傅，可能失去刚得到的接纳。他把说明放在油壶旁，提议只做一次有测量的试验。结果随断线一起变化的是温度，而非轮压。
小组请来制造商技师，重写维修卡。这一决定让生产再停一班，也使最受尊重的师傅十分难堪，因为他早已承诺迅速修好。那位师傅仍在讨论开始时亲手摆出三次失败记录。长凳上的共同语言曾让合作变快，也曾让大家只看见同一种可能原因。阿典还用自己的培训津贴支付试验布料，让这次质疑不只是一句没有成本的建议。
此后午间谈话仍继续，却加入故障记录、新人提问与外部联系。新人仍从真实但有限的任务开始，随能力和信任增加而扩大参与。一名轮值成员专门检查行话与邀请是否把夜班挡在外面。手册也没有消失：它保存长凳可能忘记的步骤，实际参与则让纸上的词获得判断。实际维修若与手册矛盾，他们会记录具体条件，不再悄悄认定纸面或记忆必有一方永远正确。
多年后，长凳换上新木板。大家保留最旧那块油黑木板，钉到维修间墙上。阿典把受热纤维的故障卡放在下面，又向旁边挪开一点，给抱着新版手册的新学徒留出座位。
explanationParagraphs: A community of practice is a group connected by a shared domain that develops knowledge and identity through sustained participation in common activities, relationships, tools, language, and problem solving. Learning often moves from legitimate limited participation toward fuller contribution. Such communities transmit tacit judgement but can exclude newcomers or reproduce error, so documentation, open entry, questioning, external evidence, and boundary connections matter.
explanationParagraphsZh: 实践共同体是一群共享领域的人，通过持续参与共同活动、关系、工具、语言与问题解决来发展知识和身份，学习常从正当的有限参与走向更充分贡献。它能传递默会判断，也可能排斥新人或复制错误，因此还需要记录、开放进入、质疑、外部证据与跨边界联系。

articles.title: The Fire Everyone Was Responsible For
articles.summary: A theatre declares fire safety everyone's duty, then watches everyone run toward the manager while smoke fills the stage.
articles.summaryZh: 剧院宣布消防人人有责，烟雾升起时，所有人却一同跑去寻找经理。
storyParagraphs: The riverside theatre painted 'Fire Safety Is Everyone's Duty' above the stage door. Manager Zhou believed the sentence created shared responsibility, so he never assigned who rang the bell, opened exits, shut lamp oil, or led the audience. During a crowded rehearsal, canvas scenery began smoking. Three people reached Zhou from different directions, each assuming someone else had sounded the alarm. Zhou had preferred the slogan because it sounded generous and spared him the uncomfortable task of assigning authority before danger arrived.

Two stagehands fetched water and collided on the narrow stair. The porter thought the stage manager had opened the side door; the stage manager thought the porter had. Musicians began directing spectators in opposite directions. The fire was contained, but the front entrance jammed and the painted moon backdrop burned through. Everyone had cared; no one had known which action was theirs first. A child dropped a shoe in the crowd, and both ushers knelt to help while no one guarded the narrowing doorway.

The theatre cancelled two performances and refunded wages it could barely afford. Zhou took the universal slogan off the backstage door and admitted that it had hidden missing interfaces. He named a first action and decision boundary for each role: the discoverer rang the bell; the stage manager stopped performance and commanded backstage; the porter opened exits and cleared zones; the lamp keeper shut oil. Every task had a backup and a handover signal. On the first draft, three names still filled the audience-count box. Zhou erased two and assigned one official count, with reports feeding it from named zones.

Clarity did not mean waiting rigidly. Anyone could report new danger; if the water lead was trapped, the nearest backup acted without seeking the highest title. Drills exposed conflict between audience counting and backstage reports, so the roles were revised. Zhou also resolved incompatible instructions: during evacuation the porter answered the safety lead, not the ticket supervisor guarding receipts. The backup rule specified when authority transferred and when it returned, so one helper at each end could not pull the crew in opposite directions.

At the next smoke drill, the first bell sent four people in four directions. One substitute took the water line when its owner pretended injury; another reported a blocked door and exercised limited authority to open the courtyard gate. No one searched for Zhou. Beneath the slogan, a board now showed names, backups, signals, and the few choices left to judgement. Afterward, each person wrote one uncertainty beside the duty board, and Zhou used those notes for the next drill.
storyParagraphsZh: 河岸剧院在后台门上写着“消防人人有责”。经理周远以为这句话已经建立共同责任，从未规定谁敲钟、谁开出口、谁关灯油、谁带观众离开。满场排练时，帆布布景开始冒烟，三个人从不同方向撞到周远身边，都以为别人已经拉响警钟。周远喜欢这句标语，因为它听来宽厚，也让他不必在危险来临前做出分配权力的棘手决定。
两名舞台工各自提水，在狭窄楼梯上撞倒；门房以为舞台主管已开侧门，舞台主管又以为门房在做。乐手们从相反方向指挥观众。火最终被控制，正门却挤成一团，画着月亮的布景也烧穿了。每个人都在意安全，却没人知道自己第一步该做什么。一个孩子在人群中掉了鞋，两名引座员都蹲下帮忙，狭窄门口反而无人维持通行。
剧院取消两场演出，退回本就难以负担的票钱。周远把那句普遍口号从后台门上揭下，承认它一直遮住了接口缺口。他为每个角色写明首要动作和决定边界：发现者敲钟，舞台主管停演并指挥后台，门房开出口和清区，灯工关闭油路。每项都有替补与交接信号。第一版安排里，观众人数那一格竟填着三个名字。周远擦掉两个，只保留一个正式总数，再由指定区域逐级回报。
清楚分工并不等于僵硬等待。任何人都可报告新危险；提水负责人受困时，最近替补无须请示最高职位。演练发现出口清点与后台报告冲突，职责便继续修改。周远还解决互不相容的命令：疏散期间，门房听安全负责人，而不是要求保护票款的售票主管。替补规则还注明权力何时转移、何时归还，免得一左一右两个帮忙者把队伍往相反方向拉。
下一次烟雾演练，第一声钟让四个人奔向四个方向。提水人假装受伤，替补立即接管；另一人发现门堵，便在有限授权内开启院门。没人再去寻找周远。旧标语下面多了一块木板，写着名字、替补、信号，以及少数必须现场判断的选择。演练结束后，每个人都在职责板旁写下一处仍不确定的地方，周远据此安排下一次测试。
explanationParagraphs: Role clarity is shared understanding of a role's purpose, responsibilities, authority, priorities, interfaces, and expected results. It reduces duplication, gaps, waiting, and conflicting assumptions. Clarity is not a rigid job box: effective roles include discretion, backups, handovers, adaptation, and mutual help. Incompatible expectations from different authorities must also be identified and resolved.
explanationParagraphsZh: 角色清晰度是成员对角色目的、责任、权力、优先级、接口与预期结果的共同理解，可减少重复、缺口、等待和冲突假设。清晰不等于僵硬岗位框，还需裁量、替补、交接、适应与互助；若不同权威提出不相容期待，也必须被识别并解决。

articles.title: The Recipe That Obeyed Only Old Flour
articles.summary: A baker who can repeat one recipe blindfolded meets flour that refuses every familiar motion.
articles.summaryZh: 闭眼也能复刻旧配方的面包师，遇见一批拒绝所有熟悉动作的新面粉。
storyParagraphs: Baker Gu Qi had made the same town loaf for twenty years. He knew the scoops of water, kneading strokes, proofing time, and oven heat without looking. That speed supplied every household before noon, and apprentices were rewarded for matching the routine. The recipe board above the table had darkened around the edges but had never needed correction.

After a flood ruined the old wheat fields, the mill delivered grain from the northern slope. Gu used the same water and motions. Dough clung to the table; the loaves emerged flat and wet. He blamed poor flour and repeated the recipe three times because past failures had usually come from apprentices departing from it. By evening, failed bread filled two baskets and the school order remained unbaked. Gu sold the failed loaves cheaply as animal feed, but the proceeds did not cover fuel or the promised school meal.

Apprentice Xiao Ning weighed old and new flour into small bowls, varied water in measured amounts, and recorded absorption, dough strength, and proofing. She predicted that the wetter new flour needed less added water and a different rest, then tested one small loaf. She did not scatter flour at random until the dough looked familiar. The trial explained which assumption in the old routine no longer held. She repeated the test with a second sack before changing the public recipe, because one sample could reflect a single damp bag.

Gu called the bowls wasteful while customers waited. Instead of buying costly old wheat to protect his reputation for speed, he cleared one table for the junior's experiments. When the school threatened to change bakers, he surrendered the morning market order, losing a week's margin, and gave one table to controlled trials. The main table still used the efficient routine for the last old sacks.

The first adjusted loaf held its shape but dried too quickly; the second tore during shaping. Xiao Ning compared them, revised one condition at a time, and asked Gu to explain why folding created strength. His long practice supplied distinctions her measurements missed. Within four days they had a stable recipe, then trained the rest of the shop until speed returned. Neither repetition alone nor unsupported improvisation had solved the new flour. Gu predicted the next result before opening the oven, then compared his prediction with the crumb rather than explaining every surprise afterward.

When the next cart arrived, Gu did not recite a water quantity. He crushed a pinch, checked the mill note, and asked an apprentice for a test bowl. The old recipe stayed above the main table. Beneath it, a smaller board now listed what to examine before deciding whether the familiar numbers applied.
storyParagraphsZh: 面包师顾齐做同一种镇面包二十年。几勺水、揉多少下、发酵多久、炉温多高，他不用看也不会错。这种速度让全镇午前都有面包，学徒只需准确复刻。桌上方的配方板边缘早被烟熏黑，内容却从未需要改动。
洪水毁掉旧麦田后，磨坊送来北坡粮。顾齐照原水量与动作操作，面团却黏在桌上，烤出的面包扁而湿。他怪面粉不合格，又连续照旧配方做三次，因为过去失败通常都来自学徒偏离步骤。傍晚，两筐坏面包堆在墙边，学校订单仍没烤出。顾齐把失败面包低价卖作饲料，所得仍补不回柴火，更填不上学校午餐的承诺。
学徒小宁把新旧面粉分别称进小碗，按测量改变水量，记录吸水、成团与发酵。她预测新粉自身含水高，所需添水更少，静置方式也应不同，然后只烤一只小面包验证。她没有随手乱撒干粉，直到面团看起来熟悉，而是找出旧流程中哪项假设不再成立。她又换第二袋重复试验，才考虑改公开配方，以免一只受潮布袋被误当成整批面粉规律。
顾齐嫌这些小碗浪费，门外顾客又在等待。他没有高价买外地旧麦来保住速度名声，而是腾出一张桌，让年轻学徒的试验拖慢作坊。学校表示将换供应者时，他放弃清晨市集订单，损失一周利润，把一张桌交给受控试做；主桌仍用最后几袋旧麦维持熟练生产。
第一只调整面包能站住，却很快变干；第二只在整形时裂开。小宁逐个比较，每次只改一项，又请顾齐说明折叠为何能增加筋力。顾齐多年的手感补上测量没看见的差别。四天后，新配方稳定，众人再共同练到恢复速度。机械重复与无依据即兴都没能独自解决新面粉。开炉以前，顾齐还必须先写下结果预测，再拿面包内部验证，不能等意外发生后才为每个结果找说法。
下一车面粉抵达时，顾齐没有先背水量。他捻碎一撮，核对磨坊批注，又叫学徒留一小碗试团。旧配方仍挂在主桌上方，下面却多了一块小板，写着在决定熟悉数字是否适用以前，先要检查哪些东西。
explanationParagraphs: Adaptive expertise combines efficient, accurate performance in familiar conditions with conceptual understanding, flexible adjustment, and responsible experimentation in unfamiliar ones. It requires strong routines and the ability to recognise when their assumptions fail. Varied cases, prediction, mechanism-based explanation, controlled tests, feedback, and reflection support adaptation; it is neither repetitive fluency alone nor unconstrained improvisation.
explanationParagraphsZh: 适应性专长结合熟悉情境中的高效准确，以及陌生情境中的概念理解、灵活调整与负责任试验。它既需要扎实惯例，也要识别惯例假设何时失效。多样案例、预测、机制解释、受控测试、反馈与反思有助于适应；它既非单纯重复熟练，也不是无约束即兴。
